# Link-or-create when processing bank-statement rows, and load the review page in one parallel fetch

## Context

The manual bank-statement review page `/bank-statements/:stmtId`
(`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala`)
is where rows are confirmed into expenses. Its "Process rows" bulk action
(`handleBulkImport`) today only ever **creates** a new expense per selected row
(or ignores it). When a row corresponds to a purchase that already has an
expense — e.g. a receipt/ticket captured earlier — processing it creates a
**duplicate**. The backend already supports linking a row to an existing expense
(`linkRowToExpense` endpoint / `LinkRowToExpenseAction`), but the page never
offers it in the bulk flow and does not even load the user's expenses.

Two changes, both scoped to this page.

## Part 1 — load everything in one parallel fetch

Today the page loads data in a `useEffect` that fires four independent
`.onComplete` calls (`getBankStatement`, `getMerchants`, `getCategories`,
`getImportRules`), with the `loading` flag gated only on the statement, so the
rest pop in late.

Replace that with a **single `AsyncComponent`** (same abstraction used elsewhere,
e.g. `BankStatementAutoReconcilePage`, the `ReCaptcha` widget) whose `fetch`
runs all of those **plus `getExpenses`** in parallel (`zip` / `Future.sequence`)
and renders the page content once, with one loading/error state. Keep the
existing AI-suggestions polling and the post-action re-fetch (the page mutates
row state after each action) inside the rendered content via a `forceRefresh`,
as the auto-reconcile page already does.

The newly-loaded expenses feed Part 2.

## Part 2 — "Process rows" links where it can

Add matching of statement rows to existing **unlinked** expenses and have the
bulk action link instead of create when there is exactly one match.

### Matching (per row, independent — no cross-row assignment)

For an eligible row (a "ready", non-ignored, debit row — `RowInfo.isReady`),
consider the user's **unlinked** expenses (`GetExpenses.Response.Expense.rowIds`
is empty). A candidate expense must satisfy **all**:

- **Date:** `expense.date <= row.date <= expense.date + 3 days` (the bank posts
  up to 3 days after the purchase).
- **Merchant/category — only when a rule resolves it:**
  - row resolves to a merchant via a rule (set_merchant / implicit merchant-name
    rule; i.e. `RowRuleVerdict.merchantId(verdict)` is defined) →
    `expense.merchantId` must equal it;
  - else row resolves to a category via a `set_category` rule (category, no
    merchant) → that category must be among the expense's split category ids;
  - else (no rule resolution — e.g. AI-only) → no merchant/category constraint.
- **Amount, in priority tiers:** tier 1 = exact (`row.amount.abs ==
  expense.amount.abs`); tier 2 = within `±1.00` absolute. Exact wins: if any
  tier-1 candidate exists, ignore tier-2 ones.

Outcome per row from the surviving candidates:
- **0 candidates →** create (unchanged behaviour).
- **exactly 1 →** link it.
- **2 or more →** ambiguous.

Put this logic in `web/.../utils/ReconciliationMatcher.scala` (shared, tested).
Note it currently keys the merchant match on the rule *pattern string* as a
proxy — switch it to the resolved `merchantId`, which the row already carries.

### "Process rows" (`handleBulkImport`)

Per selected row: Ignore verdict → ignore (unchanged); exactly one match →
`linkRowToExpense`; no match → `createExpenseFromRow` (unchanged); two or more
matches → fail that row with a clear error in the bulk results (the user is
expected to resolve ambiguous rows first via the existing "…" → "Link to
existing expense" picker — do **not** build an in-bulk picker or auto-pick).
The bulk summary reports linked / created / failed counts.

### Surfacing

On a row that has exactly one match, show a small indicator (e.g. a chip/label)
that processing it will **link to an existing expense** rather than create one,
so the outcome is visible before pressing Process. The existing per-row "…" →
"Link to existing expense" picker stays as the manual path.

## Out of scope

- The auto-reconcile page (`/bank-statements/:stmtId/auto-reconcile`) and any
  bulk auto-pairing/assignment across rows.
- No API/endpoint changes — `linkRowToExpense`, `createExpenseFromRow`,
  `getExpenses` already exist.
- No schema changes.

## Acceptance

- The review page loads statement, merchants, categories, rules and expenses
  through one parallel fetch with a single loading/error state.
- Processing a selected row that uniquely matches an existing unlinked expense
  links it (no new expense, no duplicate); a row with no match still creates;
  an ambiguous row fails with an informative error and is left unprocessed.
- Matching honours the amount tiers (exact then ±1.00), the `expense.date ..
  +3d` window, and the merchant/category constraint only when a rule resolves
  it; matching lives in `ReconciliationMatcher` with unit tests covering
  0/1/many candidates, the tier preference, the date boundary, and the
  rule-vs-no-rule constraint.
- Existing review-page behaviour (confirm, ignore, refund, manual link, rule
  creation, AI-suggestion polling) is unchanged.

resultJson.description:
The manual bank-statement review page (`/bank-statements/:stmtId`, `BankStatementReviewPage.scala`) turns statement rows into expenses. Its bulk "Process ready" action (`handleBulkImport`) only ever creates a new expense per row, or ignores it. So a row for a purchase that already has an expense (for example, a receipt captured earlier) becomes a duplicate. The backend can already link a row to an existing expense (`linkRowToExpense`). The page does not load the user's expenses, though, so it can't offer linking in the bulk flow.

This epic does two things on this page only, with no API or schema changes. (1) Data loading becomes one `AsyncComponent` whose fetch runs getBankStatement, getMerchants, getCategories, getImportRules and getExpenses in parallel, with a single loading/error state. The page body moves into a content component that re-fetches through `GenericHooks.useForceRefresh`, the same pattern as `BankStatementAutoReconcilePage`. (2) Per-row matching against the user's unlinked expenses lives in `ReconciliationMatcher` and is unit-tested. A candidate must fall in the date window `expense.date <= row.date <= expense.date + 3d`. It must match the merchant or category only when a rule resolves one. Amounts are compared in two tiers: exact first, then ±1.00. "Process rows" then links a row with exactly one match, creates for zero matches, and fails ambiguous rows with a clear error. The summary reports linked, created and failed counts. A small chip on the row shows when processing will link rather than create.

Out of scope: the auto-reconcile page's UI and flow, any assignment across rows, and an in-bulk picker for ambiguous rows (the existing "…" → "Link to existing expense" picker is the manual path). Existing behaviour must stay the same: confirm/create drawer, ignore/unignore, refund, manual link, unlink, rule creation, AI-suggestion polling and regeneration, tabs in the URL.

tasks.title: Add per-row expense matching to ReconciliationMatcher and key reconcile's merchant match on merchantId
tasks.description:
In `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ReconciliationMatcher.scala`, add a pure function, e.g. `def matchRow(row: GetBankStatement.StatementRowData, verdict: RowRuleVerdict.Verdict, expenses: List[GetExpenses.Response.Expense]): ProposedAction`. Reuse the existing `ProposedAction` ADT: `CreateNew` for 0 candidates, `AutoLink(id)` for exactly 1, `NeedsReview(ids)` for 2 or more.

Rules:
- Consider only unlinked expenses (`rowIds.isEmpty`).
- Date: `!row.date.isBefore(e.date) && !row.date.isAfter(e.date.plusDays(3))`.
- Constraint: if `RowRuleVerdict.merchantId(verdict)` is defined, require `e.merchantId == thatId`. Else if `RowRuleVerdict.categoryId(verdict)` is defined, require `e.splits.exists(_.categoryId == thatId)`. Else no constraint.
- Amount tiers: tier 1 is `row.amount.abs == e.amount.abs`; tier 2 is `(row.amount.abs - e.amount.abs).abs <= BigDecimal("1.00")`. If tier 1 is non-empty, use only tier 1.
- Use named constants for 3 days and 1.00.

Also switch `reconcile`'s SetMerchant branch from comparing the normalized rule pattern with `expense.merchantName` to comparing `expense.merchantId` with the winning rule's merchant id (`RowRuleVerdict.merchantId(RowRuleVerdict.verdict(effective, row.description))`). Remove the stale comment. Keep reconcile's other criteria as they are, so the auto-reconcile page keeps its behaviour.

Tests in `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ReconciliationMatcherSpec.scala`, new `"matchRow" should` block:
- 0, 1 and many candidates
- exact beats ±1.00, including one exact plus one near giving AutoLink(exact)
- two near candidates giving NeedsReview
- 1.01 off giving CreateNew
- date boundaries: row = expense date (accept), row = expense+3 (accept), row = expense+4 (reject), row = expense-1 (reject)
- linked expenses excluded
- SetMerchant verdict with a different merchantId rejected and with the same one accepted
- SetCategory verdict accepted only when a split has that category
- NoRule verdict matching regardless of merchant/category

Update the existing reconcile tests that relied on merchant names, e.g. 'merchant name does not match' becomes 'expense merchantId differs' and 'no merchant name' becomes 'merchantId None'. Fix the `should` subjects to drop the object name (RULE-TE-001) only in blocks you touch.

Verify: `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *ReconciliationMatcherSpec"`.

tasks.title: Load the review page through one parallel AsyncComponent fetch
tasks.description:
Restructure `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala`.

Outer `component`:
- Parse `stmtId` and render 'Invalid statement ID' on None, as `BankStatementAutoReconcilePage` does.
- Own `val (timesRefreshing, forceRefresh) = GenericHooks.useForceRefresh`.
- Render one `AsyncComponent[ReviewData]` (a small case class holding statement, merchants, categories, rules as `List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]`, and expenses). Its `fetch` starts all five client calls first, then combines them with `zip`/for-comprehension so they run in parallel. Use `progressIndicator = () => Loader(props.ctx)` and `watchedObjects = List(timesRefreshing)`.
- Let AsyncComponent render errors itself; remove the hand-made loading and 'Statement not found' branches.
- Move the existing body into a content component in the same file (e.g. `BankStatementReviewContent`, following RULE-FE-001) that takes ctx, the loaded data and `onRefresh: () => Unit`.
- Render it with `.withKey(timesRefreshing.toString)` so each re-fetch remounts it and re-seeds its `useState`s from fresh props. Without this, `useState` initialisers ignore new props.
- Because the content remounts on refresh, lift any UI state that must survive a refresh into the outer component and pass it down: toast, bulk import/ignore results and progress.

Inside the content:
- Seed `statementRows`, `rowEdits`, `merchantList`, `categoryList`, `ruleList` and `statement` from props. Keep a local copy of expenses in state for the next task (plain `useState(props.data.expenses)`; it can go unused here).
- Delete the four `.onComplete` mount loads and the `loading` flag.
- Keep the AI-suggestions polling effect, regenerate, and all optimistic per-row updates unchanged.
- Replace `refreshRow` (used after the create-expense form and the link picker) with `onRefresh()`. That full re-fetch also keeps the expense list current.
- Also call `onRefresh()` after a successful unlink, because the expense becomes unlinked again.

Pure helpers and their existing tests in `BankStatementReviewPageSpec` (`resultLabel`, `rowInfo`, `resolveImport`, etc.) must keep their signatures.

Verify:
- `CI=true sbt Test/compile`
- `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewPageSpec *BankStatementReviewRowSpec"`

tasks.title: Process rows: link a uniquely matching row, create when none match, fail when ambiguous
tasks.description:
In the review content component (after the AsyncComponent split), memoize `expenseMatchById: Map[UUID, ReconciliationMatcher.ProposedAction]` over `statementRows`, `rowInfoById` and the local expenses. Compute it only for rows where `info.isReady && info.verdict != RowRuleVerdict.Ignore && row.amount < 0`, using `ReconciliationMatcher.matchRow(row, info.verdict, expenses)`.

Rewrite the `handleBulkImport` loop. For each selected row:
- Ignore verdict: ignore it, as today.
- `AutoLink(expId)`: call `linkRowToExpense(stmtId, rowId, LinkRowToExpense.Request(expId))`. On success, update the row optimistically: `expenseId = Some(expId)`, `expenseMerchantId = expense.merchantId`, and `expenseCategoryId` = the single split's category when there is exactly one split, else None (matching how the server reports it). Also mark the expense as linked in the local expenses state by appending the rowId to `rowIds`, so it no longer matches other rows.
- `NeedsReview(ids)`: append `Left(...)` with an informative message, e.g. s"Matches ${ids.size} existing expenses — link it manually via … → Link to existing expense". Make no API call and leave the row unprocessed.
- `CreateNew`: keep the existing create path (including 'No category').

Safety guard: track expense ids linked during this run. If a row's unique match was already used earlier in the same run, fail that row with a clear message instead of linking a second row to the same expense.

Track linked, created, ignored and failed counts through the loop. When the loop ends, show a summary built by a new pure helper on `BankStatementReviewPage`, e.g. `def bulkImportSummary(linked: Int, created: Int, ignored: Int, failed: Int): String` (omit zero parts except as needed). Show the summary even when some rows failed, replacing the current 'Imported N expenses' toast. Then call `onRefresh()` so the page reloads the expense list. The summary and results must survive the refresh, i.e. live in the lifted state.

Update the progress text if needed ('Processing…'). Unit-test `bulkImportSummary` in `BankStatementReviewPageSpec`. If you extract a pure per-row decision helper (e.g. returning Ignore / Link(id) / Create / Fail(msg)), test it there too.

Verify:
- `CI=true sbt Test/compile`
- `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewPageSpec *ReconciliationMatcherSpec"`

tasks.title: Show a 'Will link to existing expense' indicator on uniquely matched rows
tasks.description:
Add a prop to `BankStatementReviewRow.Props` (`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewRow.scala`), e.g. `linksToExpense: Boolean`, or `matchedExpense: Option[UUID]` if a label is wanted. It must be a plain value so the `React.memo` props-equality check still works.

The page passes it from the memoized `expenseMatchById`: true or Some only for `AutoLink`. If the previous task has not landed, compute the map in this task in the same way: `ReconciliationMatcher.matchRow` over ready, non-Ignore, debit rows.

In the row, for an open (not linked/ignored) row with the flag set, render a small chip via the existing `tintChip` helper. Put it in the Match cell next to the merchant chip, or under the description like the `txnType` chip, e.g. '↔ Link existing'. Use theme CSS vars, not hex colours. Use `def`, not a shared `val`, for any element used twice. The primary button and the '…' menu stay unchanged.

Update the `props(...)` helper in `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewRowSpec.scala` for the new field. Add one jsdom test that the chip text renders when the flag is set and is absent otherwise. This is justified because it checks the memoized row picks up the new prop, and it follows the existing spec's style.

Verify:
- `CI=true sbt Test/compile`
- `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewRowSpec"`

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared/ — Tapir endpoints and shared models, plus `net.wiringbits.api.utils.{ImportRuleMatcher, RowRuleVerdict}` (shared rule matching) and `ApiClient` (lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/ApiClient.scala).
- web/ — Scala.js, Slinky and MUI 5 frontend. Pages are in web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/, pure utils in web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/, tests mirror these under web/src/test/scala/.
- No server or lib changes are needed: no endpoint or schema changes.

FILES
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala — the page.
  - The companion holds pure helpers that are tested in BankStatementReviewPageSpec: `statementMetadataLine`, `resultLabel(rowId, descById, Either[String,Unit])`, `suggestionsPending`, `canRegenerateSuggestions`, `ResolvedImport(merchantId: Option[UUID], categoryId: UUID, categoryFromAi: Boolean)`, `resolveImport`, `RowInfo(verdict, resolved, isReady, merchantName, categoryName, linkedMerchantName, linkedCategory)`, `rowInfo(effectiveRules, merchants, categories, aiSuggestions, row)`, `LinkedCategory`, `menuItemsFor`, `PrimaryAction`/`primaryActionFor`.
  - `component` currently loads data in a `useEffect` with 4 `.onComplete` calls and a `loading` flag. It then polls AI suggestions every 3s, capped at 20 attempts (`setStatement(cur => cur.map(_.copy(aiSuggestions=...)))`).
  - It memoizes `effectiveRuleList = ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules(ruleList, merchantList.map(m => m.id -> m.name))` and `rowInfoById: Map[UUID, RowInfo]`.
  - Handlers: handleIgnore/Unignore/Unlink/UnlinkRefund (optimistic `setStatementRows` copies), `refreshRow` (re-GETs the statement and replaces one row; used by the create-expense form and link picker onSuccess), handleBulkIgnore, and handleBulkImport (sequential recursive `loop(remaining, done, failed)` with `setBulkImportProgress(Some((done,total,failed)))` and `setBulkImportResults(cur => cur :+ (rowId -> Either))`).
  - `onRowAction` and `onToggleSelected` are `Hooks.useCallback`s, kept stable for the memoized rows.
  - The drawer hosts BankRowCreateExpenseForm, BankRowCreateRefundForm, BankRowLinkPicker (manual link; it fetches its own candidates) and BankRowRuleForm.
  - The bulk button label is "Process ready".
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewRow.scala — row component wrapped in `React.memo` with `(prev, next) => prev == next`. Props are `(row, info, selected, showCheckbox, pollingSuggestions, onToggleSelected, onAction)`. It has `tintChip(label, color)`, `matchCell` and `categoryCell` helpers. A new prop must be a plain comparable value.
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementAutoReconcilePage.scala — reference pattern: `val (timesRefreshing, forceRefresh) = GenericHooks.useForceRefresh` and `AsyncComponent[T](fetch = () => Future[T], render = t => ..., progressIndicator = () => Loader(props.ctx), watchedObjects = List(timesRefreshing))`, rendering a separate content component that receives `onRefresh`. It uses `ReconciliationMatcher.reconcile(...)`, `ProposedAction` and `qualifyingCreateRequests`. Out of scope; it must keep compiling and behaving the same apart from the merchantId keying.
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ReconciliationMatcher.scala — `sealed trait ProposedAction`; `AutoLink(expenseId)`, `NeedsReview(candidates: List[UUID])`, `CreateNew`; `qualifyingCreateRequests`; `reconcile(rows, expenses, rules, merchants): Map[UUID, ProposedAction]`, which currently matches on rule.pattern vs expense.merchantName with a symmetric ±3-day window and exact amount.
- Tests: web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ReconciliationMatcherSpec.scala (has `makeRow`/`makeExpense` builders), web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPageSpec.scala (pure-helper tests, `sampleRow`), web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewRowSpec.scala (jsdom with BrowserRouter; a `props(...)` builder needs updating if Props changes).

KEY TYPES AND APIS
- `GetBankStatement.StatementRowData(id, index, date: LocalDate, amount: BigDecimal, description, manuallyEdited, confirmedAt, expenseId: Option[UUID], refundId, ignoredAt: Option[Instant], txnType: String, expenseMerchantId: Option[UUID], expenseCategoryId: Option[UUID])`. Debit rows have amount < 0.
- `GetBankStatement.Response` has `id, statementRows, aiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions], documentFilename, bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd`.
- `GetExpenses.Response(data: List[Expense])`; `Expense(id, amount: BigDecimal (positive), date: LocalDate, time, merchantId: Option[UUID], merchantName, notes, splits: List[Split(id, categoryId, amount)], createdAt, receiptIds = Nil, rowIds = Nil)`. "Unlinked" means `rowIds.isEmpty`.
- `RowRuleVerdict.Verdict` = NoRule | Ignore | SetMerchant(merchantId) | SetCategory(categoryId). `RowRuleVerdict.merchantId(v)` and `RowRuleVerdict.categoryId(v)` return Options; `RowRuleVerdict.verdict(effectiveRules, description)` computes the verdict. Implicit merchant-name rules show up as SetMerchant once you use `ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules`. `RowInfo.verdict` is already computed against the effective rules.
- ApiClient (`props.ctx.api.client`): `getBankStatement(id): Future[GetBankStatement.Response]`, `getMerchants: Future[GetMerchants.Response]` (.data), `getCategories: Future[GetCategories.Response]` (.data), `getImportRules: Future[GetImportRules.Response]` (map with `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule.fromApi`), `getExpenses: Future[GetExpenses.Response]`, `linkRowToExpense(stmtId, rowId, LinkRowToExpense.Request(expenseId)): Future[LinkRowToExpense.Response]`, `createExpenseFromRow(stmtId, rowId, CreateExpenseFromRow.Request(amount, date, time, merchantId, notes, splits: List[CreateExpenseFromRow.Split(categoryId, amount)], receiptId))` returning `.expenseId`, `ignoreRow`, `unlinkRow`.
- Server `LinkRowToExpenseAction` refuses non-debit, already-linked or ignored rows. It does NOT stop one expense being linked to several rows, so the frontend must not double-link within one bulk run.
- Imports: `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.components.core.AsyncComponent`, `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.core.GenericHooks`, `net.wiringbits.components.widgets.Loader`.

CONVENTIONS (docs/guide/frontend.md, antipatterns.md, testing.md)
- Components follow RULE-FE-001: object with `def apply(...): KeyAddingStage`, a case class Props, and `val component = FunctionalComponent[Props]`. Pass AppContext through props; no useContext.
- Never keep a ReactElement or KeyAddingStage in an object-level val. Use `def` for elements rendered more than once. Give every mapped element `.withKey`. Use `.fold[ReactElement](Fragment())` for optional elements. No `js.Dynamic`/`asInstanceOf` in pages. Use theme CSS vars (`var(--lc-...)`), not hex.
- Hook deps: the guide prefers `""` or `List(...)`. The page currently uses `js.Array` deps in its existing effects; leave those alone unless you rewrite them.
- Use `.onComplete` for side-effecting API calls. The CLAUDE.md "No hacks" rule applies: no setTimeout ordering tricks.
- Fail loudly: an ambiguous match must become a visible per-row failure, never a guessed pick.
- Tests: ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec` with `org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers.*`. `should` subjects name the method or behaviour, not the object (RULE-TE-001). Prefer pure-function tests over DOM tests (RULE-TE-010).
- Build: `CI=true` enables -Werror (unused imports and locals fail). Run targeted tests only, e.g. `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *ReconciliationMatcherSpec"`, or typecheck with `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Don't run the full `sbt test`. Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing.
- Web tests need Node 24 on PATH; the default shell node is v16 and yarn install fails with it.

NON-OBVIOUS NOTES
- AsyncComponent re-fetches when `watchedObjects` changes. `useState` initialisers inside the rendered child do not re-read props, so key the content component on `timesRefreshing` to force a clean remount. Anything that must survive a refresh (toast, bulk results, summary) belongs in the outer component.
- The tab filter already lives in the URL (`?tab=`), so a remount keeps it. Selection is cleared after bulk runs anyway.
- `rowInfoById`'s `isReady` also counts Ignore-verdict rows. Matching must skip those, along with positive (refund) rows.
- When updating a linked row optimistically, set `expenseCategoryId` only when the expense has exactly one split; the server reports None for multi-split expenses, which the Category cell shows as "Multiple".

findings.title: No test covers the new single-fetch load or the refresh/remount behaviour

reason.text: A component spec would need a stubbed `ApiClient`. `ApiClient` is a concrete class whose constructor needs an sttp backend, there is no trait to stub, and no existing web test fakes it. The only part that could be pulled out as a pure function, building `ReviewData` from the responses, is trivial field mapping. After the I1.1/I3.1 fix, most of the listed properties (unlink calls onRefresh, results surviving a remount) no longer apply. Testing the remaining wiring needs fake-API test infrastructure, which is outside this task.

id.name: Task: Process rows: link a uniquely matching row, create when none match, fail when ambiguous
